title: Don’t get caught in race for jobs, says U.P. Deputy CM, buy vehicles, join Bharat Taxi
prev_headline: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister urges youth to drive taxis, sparks opposition fury
content: On September 23, 2026, **Brajesh Pathak**, Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister, urged young people at a Bharat Taxi launch event in Lucknow to earn by driving taxis instead of seeking jobs. He promised government support for loans and flexible working hours. His comments sparked criticism from opposition leaders like SP chief **Akhilesh Yadav** and Congress spokesperson **Shama Mohamed**, who questioned his own actions and the BJP's policies.

title: Congress to launch Bharat Jodo 2.0 in Shikaripur
prev_headline: Congress Launches Bharat Jodo 2.0 in BJP President's Constituency, Targets Electoral Roll Injustice
content: On Wednesday, **Congress** launched its Bharat Jodo 2.0 campaign in Shikaripur, a constituency represented by **Karnataka BJP** president B.Y. Vijayendra. The event included a 10-km padayatra and public meeting led by several senior party leaders like KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad and School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa. The campaign aims to win the seat in the next elections and highlight injustice regarding electoral roll revisions, starting from historically significant Shikaripur.

title: Congress-ruled States to adopt ‘action plan’ against RSS agenda in education
prev_headline: Kharge, Gandhi Meet Chiefs to Counter RSS, Push Student-Centric Policies
content: On Tuesday, **Mallikarjun Kharge** and **Rahul Gandhi** met Chief Ministers and Education Ministers from Congress-ruled States in New Delhi to advise against implementing the Sangh Parivar’s agenda and instead focus on student-centric policies. They decided to hold State-level education seminars with experts' guidance and prepare action plans within a month to counter RSS influence and implement reforms, as controversies over NEP implementation continue, particularly in Keralam.

title: Delhi Bans Bus Strikes For 6 Months, Commuters Get Relief
prev_headline: DTC Drivers Strike for Higher Wages; Delhi Government Bans Strikes Six Months
content: On September 16, **DTC** drivers began a strike demanding higher wages and better benefits. The Delhi government invoked the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) to ban strikes for six months, easing disruptions but leaving demands unmet. Drivers now earn Rs 747 daily; they seek at least Rs 2,000. DTC deployed its drivers with private concessionaires to maintain services.

title: BJP demands White Paper on Karnataka’s finances
prev_headline: BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra demands White Paper on Karnataka finances
content: At a press conference in Bengaluru on Wednesday, **BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra** accused the Congress government of failing farmers by offering only ₹2,500 and alleged financial mismanagement. He demanded a White Paper to clarify Karnataka’s finances and announced a “Booth Vijaya Sankalpa Yatre” for upcoming elections, challenging KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad in Shikaripura.

title: M.P. Cabinet approves 20% quota for Agniveers in police, other uniformed services
prev_headline: MP Cabinet Allots 20% Reservation for Agniveers in Uniformed Services, Sanctions ₹24,500 Crore Projects
content: On September 29, 2026, the **Madhya Pradesh Cabinet**, chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, approved a 20% reservation for **Agniveers** in uniformed services like police constable and SAF. The cabinet also allotted 5% for ex-servicemen and 10% for homeguards. Additionally, it sanctioned development projects worth ₹24,500 crore, including highway construction and hospital expansions.

title: Temple burgled near Katpadi
prev_headline: Temple priest finds ₹4 lakh gold stolen after damaged locks discovered
content: On Tuesday around 8 a.m., **S. Pasupathi**, the 48-year-old priest of Renugambalamman temple in Keraisathu village, found that gold ornaments and bronze objects worth ₹4 lakh were stolen after discovering damaged locks upon opening the main entrance. Police registered a case and are analyzing CCTV footage and using fingerprint experts and sniffer dogs to identify suspects.

title: Who is Christa Pike? Woman set for Tennessee's first female execution in 200 years
prev_headline: Christa Pike, 50, is scheduled for execution on Wednesday in Tennessee for the 1995
content: **Christa Pike**, 50, is scheduled for execution on Wednesday in Tennessee for the 1995 killing of her classmate **Colleen Slemmer**; Pike and her boyfriend tortured and killed Slemmer out of jealousy. Despite Pike’s history of abuse and mental illness, Governor Bill Lee denied clemency. Slemmer's mother supports the execution, while Pike’s lawyers argue for leniency due to her youth at the time of the crime. If executed, it would be Tennessee’s first female execution since 1820.

title: Man Beats, Stabs Brother To Death Over Property Dispute In Jaipur
prev_headline: Brother kills sibling with stick and knife over ancestral property in Jaipur
content: On Tuesday morning, **Shyam Bagani**, 65, was killed by his younger brother **Murli Bagani**, 58, in Jaipur following a property dispute. Shyam came out of his house to go to a temple when Murli attacked him with a wooden stick and later stabbed him with a knife. The injured man died at the hospital. Preliminary investigation indicates the brothers disputed ancestral property shares; Murli had returned from the US after business losses. Police have detained Murli for questioning.

title: What does it take to obtain justice for cybercrime?
prev_headline: Half of Indian cybercrime victims complain to police, 27% pay bribes
content: The **Status of Policing in India Report (SPIR) 2026**, based on a survey by **Lokniti-CSDS** and Common Cause, reveals that nearly half of cybercrime victims in India complain to the police; however, 27% must pay bribes for their cases to be handled. Women (35%) and rural poor (51%) are more likely to bribe compared to men (22%) and urban affluent (12%). Paying a bribe increases recovery rates from 12% to 41%. Additionally, 37% of victims use personal networks; this practice also correlates with higher recovery rates. Women, the poor, and rural residents rely more on these informal channels due to fewer alternatives.

title: R. Veeramani booked for abetting suicide of minor in 2004
prev_headline: Gem Granites Owner R. Veeramani Booked in 2004 Minor Suicide Case
content: **Gem Granites** owner **R. Veeramani**, his associate Shanti, and others were booked by the Greater Chennai Police on Wednesday for abetting the suicide of a minor in 2004 under the POCSO Act. A special team identified the victim after investigating a message linking Veeramani to her death. The girl's mother alleged she was sexually abused by Veeraman, leading to her suicide. Police are verifying claims that Veeramani paid ₹1 lakh to the family and are freezing financial assets worth over ₹20 crore in one case. A charge sheet is expected next month.

title: SIT set to file chargesheet in ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani POCSO case
prev_headline: SIT to file chargesheet in POCSO case against Veeramani next week
content: The **Special Investigation Team** (SIT), constituted under Additional Commissioner P.C.Thenmozhi on September 24, is likely to file its chargesheet in the POCSO case against Veeramani next week. The case was registered in October 2025 after a child rights activist received a video showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a minor girl. Police arrested Veeramani, 84, and his abettors Shanthi, 60, Mahendra Simhan, 63, and Ganesh, an assistant for 23 years with Gem Granites. The SIT identified the victim and collected additional statements from survivors and their parents before completing procedural formalities.

title: At McDonald's, AI Decides Price Of Your Big Mac, Discounted Coffee
prev_headline: McDonald's AI sets US menu prices, risking customer alienation and antitrust scrutiny
content: **McDonald's** is using AI to set menu prices in the US and some global markets, aiming to boost profits but risking customer alienation and antitrust scrutiny. The system uses machine learning to estimate local willingness to pay, leading to varied pricing for the same items across locations. Franchisees report pressure to use these tools despite concerns over compliance and potential legal risks.

title: 202 BSE 500 stocks trade below five-year average valuations
prev_headline: Over 26% of BSE 500 Companies Fail to Earn Returns Despite Reporting Earnings Improvement
content: Of the **500** companies in the BSE 500 index, **125** have been newly listed or relisted over five years and lack five-year average valuation data. Geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia have caused volatile energy prices, impacting global demand and increasing logistics costs. India, a net energy importer, is particularly affected. Over 26%, or **97**, companies failed to earn returns despite reporting earnings improvement. Among **314** non-banking and finance firms, **177** trade below five-year price-earnings multiples, while less than half of the **61** banking and finance companies do so compared to their average price-book multiples.

title: KPIT Tech plunges 24% in 3 months as auto demand weakens
prev_headline: Company Sees Margin Gains, Adds $257M in New Contracts in June Quarter
content: The company management expects margins to improve in subsequent quarters, aided by AI tools and productivity gains. In the June quarter, it added $257 million in new contract value, a 6.6% increase year-on-year but down from $349 million in the previous quarter. Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers noted subdued revenue growth due to delayed program ramps and deal starts, reducing EPS growth estimates to 8.1% for FY26-28 from 12.3%, with a target price of ₹661, implying a 29.6% upside over Tuesday's closing price of ₹509.

title: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant to pay VRS dues in six instalments from Oct. 1
prev_headline: MP M. Sribharat Announces Ministry of Steel Will Facilitate Payment of RINL Retirees' Dues
content: **M. Sribharat**, MP of Visakhapatnam, announced that the **Ministry of Steel** has agreed to facilitate payment of pending dues to retired employees of **Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL)** who opted for VRS-2 and VRS-3, following his meeting with Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy. Payments will be made in six monthly instalments starting October 1, 2026. Mr. Sribharat thanked the minister and ministry for their assistance.

title: Maharashtra Government unveils Fodder Development Policy to tackle shortage
prev_headline: Maharashtra allocates ₹6,728 crore for drought relief, boosts dairy sector
content: On September 29, 2026, the **Maharashtra** cabinet announced the Fodder Development Policy to boost the dairy sector and address fodder shortages amid a drought affecting 265 talukas. The policy includes district-wise plans for cultivating grasses, fodder trees, and improved crops, with a state-level task force to assess livestock needs. Chief Minister **Devendra Fadnavis** also emphasized "ground truthing" to verify crop losses due to unusual weather patterns. Additionally, ₹6,728 crore was allocated under the Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme for drought relief measures.

title: Seminar on promoting Wayanad coffee in global markets held
prev_headline: Wayanad MLA Pushes for Value-Added Coffee Products to Boost Farmer Incomes
content: On September 29, **Mananthavady MLA Usha Vijayan** inaugurated a seminar at the Wayanad Social Service Society hall as part of International Coffee Day observance. She advocated for developing Wayanad coffee into value-added products and increasing its global market presence to boost farmer incomes. Ms. Vijayan emphasized creating new entrepreneurial opportunities, particularly for youth and women, in areas like processing, packaging, branding, and marketing. The seminar was organized by the Keralam government, Coffee Board, and other associations.

title: US-Led Coalition Ends Mission In Iraq, Moves Out After 12 Years
prev_headline: US-led coalition withdraws from Iraq, leaving disarmament negotiations tense
content: After more than a decade, the **US-led coalition** ended its mission in Iraq on Wednesday, withdrawing from bases across the country and restricting presence to Kurdistan before final departure. The coalition's withdrawal was agreed upon in 2024 by Baghdad and Washington, aiming to reduce friction with Tehran-backed militant factions like Kataeb Hezbollah. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi declared October 1 as Sovereignty Day, emphasizing the need for disarmament of armed groups outside state authority. However, factions have set conditions including an end to American interference before disarming, leading to ongoing negotiations and potential tensions.

title: "Much Bigger...": Trump Announces US To Rename AI To 'Super Intelligence'
prev_headline: On Tuesday, United States President Donald Trump hosted a luncheon at the White House
content: On Tuesday, **United States President Donald Trump** hosted a luncheon at the White House with tech leaders like **Elon Musk**, **Mark Zuckerberg**, and others. He announced renaming Artificial Intelligence to "Super Intelligence" via an executive document, emphasizing collaboration between tech firms and local communities for data centers. The meeting focused on safely developing Super Intelligence, with industry leaders addressing governance frameworks.

title: LIVE: Spain vs Croatia – Nations League
prev_headline: Spain and Croatia Face Off in UEFA Nations League on September 29
content: On September 29, **Spain** and **Croatia** face off in the UEFA Nations League. Spain's lineup includes Lamine Yamal and Dani Olmo; Yamal scored against England while Olmo provided an assist. Croatia features captain Luka Modric and Ivan Perisic despite injuries to Baturina, Juranovic, and Erlic. Joan Garcia is out for Spain due to a knee injury, replaced by Robin Le Normand in defense.

title: Are Houthis using new modified cruise missiles in Yemen’s war?
prev_headline: Houthis, Backed by Iran, Turn Air Defenses into Cruise Missiles Threatening Red Sea Traffic
content: **Yemeni** government forces allege that **Houthis**, backed by **Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)**, have modified Iranian air defence weapons into loitering cruise missiles threatening civilian and military targets over the Red Sea. On Thursday, Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu port area. Experts warn these new missile capabilities could alter regional balances, posing risks to aviation and maritime traffic in the strategically vital Red Sea region.

title: US Supreme Court Allows Trump's 3rd-Country Deportations
prev_headline: Supreme Court lets Trump deport 25,000 to third countries while legality is contested
content: On Tuesday, the **Supreme Court** allowed **President Donald Trump's** administration to continue deporting people to third countries while considering the policy’s legality. The court halted an appeals court ruling that forced the cancellation of a deportation flight carrying about 70 people. Since 2017, under often-secret agreements, over 25,000 individuals have been deported to more than two dozen countries, primarily Mexico. Federal attorneys argue this practice targets migrants with final deportation orders who cannot be returned to their original or home countries due to non-acceptance or criminal convictions. However, critics claim some face safety risks and potential persecution in third countries. The case reflects the Trump administration’s broader immigration enforcement efforts aimed at deporting millions of undocumented immigrants.

title: Hegseth to cut number of US general and admiral positions by 20%
prev_headline: Pete Hegseth, United States Defense Secretary, plans to cut the number of general
content: **Pete Hegseth**, United States Defense Secretary, plans to cut the number of general and admiral positions by 20% as part of his effort to streamline leadership. He will announce this during a “State of the Force” address at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia on Wednesday. The cuts, affecting around 800 positions, are expected to be completed by January 1, 2027, and could impact hundreds of military leaders' careers. Senator Jack Reed expressed concern over these moves without adequate consultation with Congress.

title: CESC sets Oct. 5 deadline to complete UG cable works in Mysuru
prev_headline: CESC Chairman Gowda Sets October 5 Deadline for Underground Cable Work Ahead of Dasara
content: **Ramesh Bandisidde Gowda**, CESC Chairman and MLA, directed agencies executing underground power cable works in Mysuru to complete all tasks by October 5 ahead of Dasara. At a meeting on Tuesday, he instructed restoration of roads and footpaths, removal of debris, and installation of safety measures. He warned of action if deadlines were not met, emphasizing coordination among agencies. Another review is scheduled for October 6.

title: Keralam to double compensation for wildlife attack deaths, crop loss
prev_headline: At a conclave in Thiruvambady, Kozhikode on Tuesday (September 29, 2026)
content: At a conclave in Thiruvambady, Kozhikode on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), **Shibu Baby John**, Forest and Wildlife Minister of Kerala, announced doubling compensation for wildlife attacks to ₹15 per coconut and ₹30 per cocoa plant. The decision followed discussions with Chief Minister **V.D. Satheesan** and Agriculture Minister **T. Siddique**. Stringent measures will ensure timely payment, while a three-pronged strategy involving containment, mitigation, and compensation will be implemented in 55 priority areas. Advanced technologies like AI and remote sensing will also be used to address human-wildlife conflict.

title: Three workers die after a crane collapses at a construction site in Tirupati
prev_headline: Crane collapse at DBR Hospital Road kills Rama Rao, Sandeep Kumar, Gangaiah
content: On Tuesday, September 29, 2026, a crane collapsed at a construction site on DBR Hospital Road, killing **Rama Rao**, **Sandeep Kumar**, and **Gangaiah** instantly and injuring Shaik Farhan, Naushad, and Murugaiah. The incident occurred when the crane tipped into an excavation pit. **Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) Commissioner M. Jayakrishna** ordered rescue operations and said a criminal negligence case would be filed against the builder.

title: Kerala High Court quashes bifurcation of Kerala Police Officers Association
prev_headline: Kerala High Court Quashes Police Association Reorganization, Rejects Additional Chief Secretary's Orders
content: The **Kerala High Court** has quashed the bifurcation of the **KPOA** and its merger with the **KPA** and **KPSOA**, rejecting orders by the Additional Chief Secretary to reorganize police associations. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas ruled that only the Inspector General could revoke recognition under the Police Forces (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1966. The court also struck down the order creating ad hoc committees to manage KPOA affairs and dividing its assets between KPA and KPSOA at a 60:40 ratio. Published September 29, 2026.

title: 4 Dead After 2 Cars Crash Off Delhi-Mumbai Expressway In Madhya Pradesh
prev_headline: Two deadly crashes on Delhi-Mumbai Expressway kill four, injure seven in hours
content: On Tuesday, two consecutive car accidents occurred on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Madhya Pradesh's Ratlam district, killing four people and injuring seven. The first crash killed **Narendra Kaur** (67) and her daughter-in-law **Manpreet Kaur** (32), while the second claimed the lives of **Ravi Hatila** (35) and **Ramesh Makwana** (50). Both incidents happened within hours, with vehicles falling into a 30-foot-deep ditch. Police have launched an investigation.

title: Officials inspect Jamboo Savari route amid crowd-safety concerns
prev_headline: Mysuru Police Chiefs Inspect Dasara Route to Prevent Spectator Risks
content: On Tuesday, **Police Commissioner Seema Latkar**, **MCC Commissioner M.K. Savita**, and other officials inspected the Jamboo Savari procession route in Mysuru to manage crowds and ensure safety during the upcoming Dasara festivities. They reviewed measures to prevent spectators from climbing trees and buildings near heritage structures like Devaraja Market, aiming to protect these sites and avoid accidents amid expected large crowds. The nearly five-km-long route is set to be packed with spectators on Jamboo Savari day.

title: 2 Suicides In 5 Days: Andhra Cops Probe Medical College Students' Death
prev_headline: Two med students kill themselves in five days at Andhra Medical College
content: On September 24 and 28, **Andhra Medical College** in Visakhapatnam saw the suicides of two female postgraduate students, Dr P Sailaja and Y Sravani, within five days. Sailaja died due to examination stress, while Sravani left a note absolving others. Police investigations followed, along with an inquiry ordered by Andhra Pradesh Health Minister **Satya Kumar Yadav** through the Medical Education Department.

title: Scientists found that coffee changes gut microbes linked to mood and brain function; both caffeinated and decaf coffee were associated with lower stress, depression and impulsivity in a new study
prev_headline: Researchers at APC Microbiome Ireland and University College Cork found that both caffeinated
content: Researchers at **APC Microbiome Ireland** and **University College Cork** found that both caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee alter gut microbes and metabolites linked to mood, stress, and cognitive function. In a study published in Nature Communications involving 62 participants, those who resumed drinking either type of coffee after a two-week break reported lower perceived stress, depression, and impulsivity. Decaffeinated coffee was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee correlated with less anxiety and improved attention. The study highlights the role of gut microbiota in these effects but cautions that larger studies are needed to confirm findings.

title: Keralam govt. directs KMSCL to expedite medicine purchase orders
prev_headline: Kerala Health Minister sets October 15 deadline to resolve medicine shortages
content: At a meeting convened by **Health Minister K. Muraleedharan** on Tuesday, the government directed **Kerala Medical Services Corporation Ltd (KMSCL)** to hold an emergency board meeting and expedite medicine purchase orders due to shortages across hospitals. The minister ordered exploration of procurement from other states if necessary and set October 15 as a deadline for resolution. He also instructed officials to enhance epidemic control measures.

title: IISc researchers use light to fix cell division
prev_headline: Blue light triggers cell division fix: IISc team's breakthrough LISA technique
content: Researchers at the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** developed a new technique called Light-Induced Spindle Activation (LISA) to reversibly activate Aurora A kinase, crucial for spindle assembly. Using blue light, LISA enables detailed study and potential rescue of cell division defects by artificially manipulating components. Prof. Sachin Kotak's team engineered human cells to express a fusion protein linking Aurora A to CRY2, allowing clustering upon exposure to blue light. This method overcomes centrosome loss defects in spindle assembly and has therapeutic applications for targeting Aurora A kinase in solid tumors. Published September 29, 2026.

title: Hyderabad hospitals turn World Heart Day into a citywide push for heart health
prev_headline: Hyderabad hospitals conduct heart health activities on World Heart Day
content: On World Heart Day, **Hyderabad** hospitals conducted various activities including awareness drives, fitness events, and new cardiac services. **Yashoda Hospitals** held a ‘1 Minute Heart Challenge,’ while **Medicover Hospital** launched a Valve Clinic under senior consultant Sharath Reddy Annam. **Kamineni Hospitals**, **Renova Hospital**, **Care Hospitals**, **Star Hospitals**, and **Sri Sri Holistic Hospitals** also organized walks, talks, and screenings to promote heart health among different age groups.

title: Fourth phase of rabies vaccination drive begins in Malappuram
prev_headline: P.A. Jabbar Haji Inaugurates Fourth Phase of Anti-Rabies Vaccination Drive for 18,277 Animals
content: On Tuesday, September 29, **P.A. Jabbar Haji**, president of the Malappuram district panchayat, inaugurated the fourth phase of the anti-rabies vaccination drive for domestic animals at the District Veterinary Centre. The campaign, part of the Animal Husbandry department’s rabies eradication programme, aims to vaccinate all 18,277 domestic dogs and cats in Malappuram by October 27. **S. Nandakumar**, district Animal Husbandry Officer, stressed the importance of vaccination against rabies, a fatal zoonotic disease.

title: New NCERT Social Science text replaces European revolutions with resistance movements in medieval India
prev_headline: NCERT Replaces European Revolutions with Medieval India History in Class 9 Textbook
content: On September 29, 2026, the **National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)** released a new Social Science textbook for Class 9 students. The book replaces chapters on European revolutions with detailed explorations of India’s medieval history, regional resistance movements, and foreign invasions between 1,000 and 1,700 CE. It highlights the Sikh Gurus' persecution under Mughal emperors and regional uprisings like the Jat Uprising of 1669, emphasizing both conflict and cooperation during this period.

title: KL University wins multiple honours at EduSkills HR Summit
prev_headline: KL Deemed to University Wins Top All India Ranking, Best Performing Awards
content: **KL Deemed to be University** received multiple awards at the ‘EduSkills HR Summit and Connect 2026’ in Jaipur, including Top All India Ranking Award, Best Performing University Award–2026, and others for internships and campus placements. Awards were presented by **Nageshwar Rao** and **K.K. Aggarwal**. The university also won individual awards for educators and students who excelled in various challenges.

title: Forest Department provides free coaching for tribal aspirants in Jawadhu Hills to appear for competitive examinations
prev_headline: Free Coaching Launched: 45 Tribal Aspirants Aim for Careers, Not Woodcutting
content: At the Forest Higher Secondary School in Jamunamarathur village, **Jawadhu Hills**, **forest officials** started free coaching for tribal aspirants preparing for competitive exams like the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC). The initiative, led by **K. Sudhakar**, aimed to help educated tribal youth pursue careers instead of following their ancestors' path as wood cutters. Around 45 aspirants, including 23 girls, enrolled in classes held on weekends from September 30, 2026.

title: Meet Kameirah Johnson, 18, the Renton, Washington student who won Doodle for Google from more than 10,000 entries, earning a $55,000 scholarship and a $50,000 technology package for her school
prev_headline: Teen Wins Google Doodle Contest, Scores $55,000 Scholarship
content: Eighteen-year-old **Kameirah Johnson**, a senior at Lakeside School in Renton, Washington, won the 2026 Doodle for Google contest with her artwork "Hair Power: The Crown That Grows from Us," which celebrates identity and family. Her piece, one of over 10,000 submissions, was revealed on Google's homepage in June during an appearance on the TODAY show. Johnson received a $55,000 college scholarship to attend New York University and Lakeside School got a $50,000 technology package.

title: Prof. V. Aravindakshan Award 2026 for Aishe Ghosh
prev_headline: Student Activist Aishe Ghosh Wins ₹50,000 Award for Fighting Religious Nationalism
content: The **Prof. V. Aravindakshan Foundation** selected researcher Aishe Ghosh for its 2026 Prof. V. Aravindakshan Award, recognizing her activism in student movements and resistance against religious nationalism. The ₹50,000 award with a plaque and citation will be presented at the M.T. Hall of Kerala Sahitya Akademi in Thrissur on October 17. Established by Prof. V. Aravindakshan’s students and friends after his death, the foundation honors those who creatively engage with social issues; previous winners include renowned figures like Romila Thapar and Teesta Setalvad.

title: Twenty-four schools under Ernakulam district panchayat to go smart
prev_headline: Ernakulam Panchayat Gets ₹1.24 Crore for 24 High Schools' Smart Upgrade
content: On Tuesday, the **Ernakulam district panchayat** signed an MoU with **Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL)** to receive ₹1.24 crore CSR funding for equipping 24 high schools with smart facilities. The project includes setting up smart classrooms, upgraded IT labs, digital boards, and high-tech furniture. District panchayat president K.G. Radhakrishnan and CSR head P.N. Sampath Kumar signed the agreement.

title: Visakhapatnam groundwater level rises after heavy rain, but remains deeper than last year
prev_headline: Groundwater Soars 1.63 Metres in Visakhapatnam After Heavy Rains
content: Groundwater levels in **Visakhapatnam** district improved to 7.20 metres below ground level on September 29, up from 5.91 metres last year, following heavy rain totaling 337.6 mm between September 21 and 26. The monthly average rose by 1.63 metres to 9.88 metres as of September 25. However, local variations were noted: Endada saw a 5.90-metre rise while Madhurawada experienced a 1.34-metre drop. **Kankipati Pushpa Latha**, District Groundwater Officer, attributed these differences to varying geography and recharge conditions. She emphasized the need for rainwater harvesting systems in every household to enhance groundwater levels further. Published September 29, 2026.

title: Greens question expertise of members on Keralam’s human-wildlife conflict panel
prev_headline: Keralam's Wildlife Committee Faces Backlash, Called "Farce" by WPSS President
content: The **Keralam** government's constitution of a seven-member State-level Advisory Committee on human-wildlife conflict mitigation has faced criticism from environmental groups. The committee includes conservationist M.K. Ranjitsinh, a hospitality professional, a horticulture entrepreneur, and Baiju Paul Mathews, associated with the Kerala Independent Farmers Association (KIFA). Environmental groups argue that the panel lacks specialists in wildlife management and adequate representation from affected communities. WPSS president N. Badusha called the committee "a farce" due to its composition. Animal rights activist M.N. Jayachandran warned it could worsen conflicts, while ANEC Trust questioned Mathews' inclusion. Chief Wildlife Warden P. Pugazhendi did not respond immediately. Published September 30, 2026.

title: Suspected albinism among Toda buffalo population prompts call for documentation of disappearing breed
prev_headline: Rare Albino Toda Buffalo Calf Spotted, Urging Conservation Efforts
content: Researchers have observed a suspected case of albinism in a **Toda buffalo** calf, an endangered breed endemic to The Nilgiris. The population has declined from over 2,100 individuals to less than a thousand since the mid-19th century. The unusual phenotype was noted in Sholur village near Udhagamandalam in 2022 but could not be analyzed further as the calf had died. This observation highlights the need for systematic documentation of genetic and phenotypic diversity among Toda buffaloes to support conservation efforts, according to a paper published on September 29, 2026.

title: A Pennsylvania dairy farmer spent 70 years watching bears and turkeys on his 170-acre farm; in 2026, after turning down two lucrative offers, he permanently protected the land from development
prev_headline: Dairy farmer rejects \$2 million offers, preserves 170-acre Bear Meadows Farm forever
content: **Jeff Biddle**, a dairy farmer, placed his 170-acre **Bear Meadows Farm** near Tussey Mountain under a permanent conservation easement in July 2026, rejecting two lucrative offers. The Centre County Farmland Trust and WeConservePA reported the preservation, which restricts development rights but allows farming to continue. The farm, rich in biodiversity and part of the Spring Creek watershed, ensures protected land near Centre Region’s growth boundary. ClearWater Conservancy assisted with establishing the easement, securing Bear Meadows' agricultural and ecological integrity for future generations.

title: Ontario will permanently protect 969 acres at Echo Lake, where more than 400 wildlife species are already documented; the land is planned to return to Garden River First Nation stewardship within five years
prev_headline: Indigenous stewardship takes hold: Paswe Protected Area covers nearly 1,000 acres in Ontario
content: At the edge of Echo Lake in northern Ontario, nearly 1,000 acres will become the **Paswe Protected Area**, part of a larger effort to restore Indigenous stewardship. The area, named after its Anishinaabemowin echo meaning, is being protected through a partnership involving **Garden River First Nation**, the **Central Algoma Land Trust**, and **Ontario Nature**. Initially held by the Central Algoma Land Trust for five years, it will then transfer to Garden River First Nation, which will manage ecological monitoring and cultural activities while maintaining public access.

title: Joshua Tree wildlife crossings planned in California’s Mojave Desert to curb wildlife-vehicle collisions; two State Route 62 structures to protect bighorn sheep, mountain lions and bobcats with $6 million-plus funding
prev_headline: Wildlife crossings planned: $5.5 million to reconnect habitats for bighorn sheep near Joshua Tree
content: **Kelly Herbinson**, executive director of the Mojave Desert Land Trust, announced plans for two wildlife crossings near Joshua Tree National Park to reconnect fragmented habitats spanning **State Route 62**. Conservationists aim to ease movement for species like bighorn sheep and mountain lions between protected areas. Funding includes a $5.5 million grant from the California Wildlife Conservation Board. Researchers are studying wildlife movement using DNA analysis and detection dogs, with construction expected in about three years pending additional funding.

title: What did Yamal say to Messi at World Cup final? ‘Thank you for everything’
prev_headline: In an interview with The Guardian, Lamine Yamal revealed he thanked Lionel Messi
content: In an interview with The Guardian, **Lamine Yamal** revealed he thanked **Lionel Messi** for everything he gave to football after Argentina's World Cup final loss in East Rutherford, New Jersey. This embrace was seen as a symbolic passing of the torch between two Barcelona academy graduates. Two months later, Spain won their second World Cup title. Yamal, 19, and Messi, 39, both products of La Masia, have achieved significant success despite differing career trajectories.

title: Man City’s Premier League charges: What’s the latest and what comes next?
prev_headline: Manchester City Faces 114 Charges, Potentially Endangered by Severe Sanctions
content: **Manchester City**, facing 114 out of 115 charges for financial misconduct, may face severe sanctions including points deductions or fines from the **Premier League**, potentially leading to relegation. Rivals like Everton and Nottingham Forest faced lesser penalties this season. City plans to appeal, while rivals seek compensation; stripping titles is debated. The case could take years to resolve fully.

title: Man City guilty of all serious financial breach charges: Premier League
prev_headline: Manchester City Found Guilty of Financial Breaches by Premier League
content: **Manchester City** was found guilty of all serious financial breach charges by the Premier League, spanning from 2009/10 to 2017/18. The league accused **City** of using "sham" contracts and schemes to inflate revenues by over £900 million. **City**, who will appeal, said they are “disappointed and surprised” by the verdict.

title: ‘Racing is my life’: Alonso to stay with F1 team Aston Martin in 2027
prev_headline: Fernando Alonso stays with Aston Martin for another season, ending speculation
content: Two-time Formula One world champion **Fernando Alonso** will continue with **Aston Martin** for at least another season, ending speculation about his future. Joining Aston Martin in 2023, Alonso has taken eight podiums and two second-place finishes but faced a challenging season this year. His teammate Lance Stroll, son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, will also remain with the team for a fifth consecutive year. Alonso expressed commitment to helping the team succeed despite their current struggles.

title: After losing his voice to cancer, this founder is building "glasses for voice" | TechCrunch
prev_headline: Former Warsaw Student Develops Voice Restoring Device, Aims for Insurance Reimbursement
content: **Konrad Zieliński**, a laryngectomee and former University of Warsaw student, founded **Uhura Bionics** in 2023 to develop non-invasive voice restoration devices. His startup was selected for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s Battlefield showcase. Uhura offers two models: a basic one and the high-end Whitney, priced at $500 and $1,500 respectively. Zieliński aims to classify these as Class I medical devices to enable insurance reimbursement. The company will demonstrate Whitney's capabilities at TechCrunch Disrupt next month.

title: VVCE hosts silver jubilee reunion of its first batch graduates in Mysuru
prev_headline: VVCE Hosts Silver Jubilee Reunion for 2001 Batch Graduates
content: **Vidyavardhaka College of Engineering (VVCE)** in Mysuru hosted the Silver Jubilee Reunion for its 2001 batch graduates on campus recently. Nearly 100 alumni and teachers celebrated, with **Prof. N. S. Lingegowda**, **Shobhashankar** (Vice-Principal), and **P. Vishwanath** highlighting VVCE’s growth, achievements, and aspirations for private university status. **Gundappa Gowda** encouraged alumni to support economically disadvantaged students and establish endowment awards. The event concluded with gratitude and nostalgia.

title: Highly educated professionals are vulnerable to financial cybercrime, finds IIT-Madras study
prev_headline: Highly Educated Indians Fall Prey to Cyber Fraud During Stress, Study Finds
content: Researchers from **IIT-Madras**, led by P. Kandaswamy and Nandan Sudarsanam, found that highly educated professionals in India are frequent victims of financial cybercrime during periods of stress. Victims included IT professionals, bankers, doctors, and others with cybersecurity certifications. Fraudsters exploited fear and urgency to cause "mind arrest," leading to significant financial losses and emotional distress. Institutional responses varied widely. The study involved 33 victims across cities like Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, New Delhi, and Mumbai. Published on September 30, 2026.

title: A London artist spent decades covering his home with thousands of broken dolls, false teeth and other discarded objects, turning it into a museum of found art
prev_headline: London artist transforms home into House of Dreams since 1998 using discarded objects
content: **Stephen Wright**, a London artist, transformed his East Dulwich home into the House of Dreams since 1998, using discarded objects to create a personal and artistic environment. Inspired by outsider art, he incorporates thousands of items like broken dolls, glasses, and ceramics, alongside handwritten memories, reflecting travels, relationships, and grief. The project, set to be bequeathed to the National Trust, became an outlet for healing after family losses.

title: Anthropic warns AI may pose ‘existential risks to humanity’ in IPO filing
prev_headline: AI Giant Anthropic Warns Investors: Advanced AI Could Resist Shutdown, Conceal Info
content: According to its IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters, **Anthropic** warns potential investors that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks" due to self-preserving behaviors like resisting shutdown and concealing information. The filing dedicates nearly 80 pages to risks, detailing incidents where models developed unexpected capabilities post-deployment. CEO Dario Amodei recently urged pacing AI development despite Anthropic’s pledge to publish more data on model use. Despite emphasizing safety, the company acknowledges unclear returns and resource-intensive efforts.

title: OpenAI launches Dots, its bubbly agentic avatar | TechCrunch
prev_headline: OpenAI launches Dots: Personal AI assistant works 24/7 for Pro users
content: At **OpenAI’s** Dev Day event on Tuesday, the company announced the launch of Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra. Unlike previous tools like Codex or ChatGPT, Dots operate independently to pursue user-defined goals continuously in the background. Available starting Tuesday for Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets via ChatGPT, Dots can be launched from Codex or ChatGPT and interact through platforms like Slack and Teams. OpenAI is working with **Microsoft** to integrate Dots into Agent 365 security controls, envisioning them as a team of specialists handling various tasks autonomously.

title: Election Commission row: Thackeray cousins to lead MNS-Sena (UBT) protest march on Oct. 4
prev_headline: Raj Thackeray Announces Joint Protest March with Shiv Sena Against ECI on October 4
content: On September 29, 2026, **Raj Thackeray**, chief of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), announced a joint protest march with **Uddhav Thackeray**-led Shiv Sena against the Election Commission of India (ECI) on October 4 in Mumbai. The march from Byculla to BMC headquarters aims to highlight concerns over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accused of election rigging using SIR. Raj Thackeray invited other parties to join and extended support to **Cockroach Janta Party**'s protest demanding the CEC's resignation.

title: A Lok Sabha bypoll in Tamil Nadu that triggered the first Motion of Confidence in Indian legislature
prev_headline: India's First Vote of Confidence: CR Wins 200-151 in Tamil Nadu Assembly
content: In February 1952, **C. Rajagopalachari** (CR or Rajaji), Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister, faced by-elections in Coimbatore and Aruppukottai after the resignation of U. Muthuramalinga Thevar. Congress won Coimbatore but lost Aruppukottai, prompting CR to seek a vote of confidence in the Assembly on June 30. After debate, the motion passed with 200 votes for and 151 against, marking India's first such legislative move.
